definitions.explanation: The physical field produced by moving electric charges and time-varying currents, encompassing both electric and magnetic components. A core concept in classical electromagnetism.

examples.japanese: {電磁場|でんじば}を{計測|けいそく}した。
{電磁場|でんじば}は{電場|でんば}と{磁場|じば}から{成|な}り{立|た}つ。
examples.english: An electromagnetic field consists of an electric field and a magnetic field.

examples.japanese: マクスウェル{方程式|ほうていしき}は{電磁場|でんじば}の{振|ふる}る{舞|ま}いを{記述|きじゅつ}する。
examples.english: Maxwell's equations describe the behavior of the electromagnetic field.

notes:
Compound of {電磁|でんじ} (electromagnetic) + {場|ば} (field). The {場|ば} element is the standard physics term for a field.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電磁場|でんじば}の{強|つよ}さ: strength of an electromagnetic field
- {電磁場|でんじば}を{発生|はっせい}させる: to generate an electromagnetic field
- {電磁場|でんじば}{理論|りろん}: electromagnetic field theory

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {電場|でんば}: electric field — only the electric component
- {磁場|じば}: magnetic field — only the magnetic component
- {重力場|じゅうりょくば}: gravitational field — the gravity analogue
- {電磁波|でんじは}: electromagnetic wave — propagating disturbance of the field
